content.title: What last year’s Oscar winners did next
content.text: A lot rides on tonight, as the stars assemble on the red carpet for the Oscars, with Leonardo DiCaprio going up against Timothée Chalamet for best actor. But when the parties and adulation are over, how much will you remember? Do you even remember who won last year? Matt Damon thinks the best way to judge a film is ten years after it is released and says the Academy Awards should be decided a decade later. So what happened to the winners of 2025? The rising star — Mikey Madison, best actress, Anora Mikey Madison dedicated her Oscars acceptance speech to the sex workers who inspired Anora. The 26-year-old beat Demi Moore and Cynthia Erivo to the award with a spirited and moving performance as a stripper who marries the son of a Russian oligarch. It was her first big lead — she was in Charles Manson’s gang in Once Upon a Time In… Hollywood — making her the first best actress winner in a decade, since Brie Larson won for Room, who was not a household name. She is using the victory to her advantage, showing that winning an Oscar means you don’t have to say yes to everything. She made her priorities clear not long after her win by walking away from a chance to enter the Star Wars universe with a role in the spin-off film Starfighter, after a salary dispute (reportedly her team were looking for a multimillion dollar deal after her Oscar), and is filming A24’s The Masque of the Red Death in Budapest, stepping into a role originally meant for Sydney Sweeney. Biggest of the bunch, though, is her role in The Social Reckoning, Aaron Sorkin’s eagerly awaited sequel to The Social Network, as the real-life Facebook whistleblower Frances Haugen — the sort of film that is likely to book Madison a place on the Oscars list next year. The perfectionist— Adrien Brody, best actor, The Brutalist Adrien Brody appears to have channelled the essence of his role as an exacting architect in The Brutalist by not having accepted a new film role since his win. “It’s not because I have not had interesting opportunities, but it didn’t feel quite right,” he said. He is not the first recent winner to take things slow — Cillian Murphy, who won in 2023, recently said he had not been on set for 15 months. Instead, Brody has debuted his solo art show Made in America at the Eden Gallery in New York — reviews of his pop-art collages showing rats and the subway were damning, with one calling it “genuinely terrible”. A year on, he’s ready to act again, preparing to step on to the Broadway stage for the first time in The Fear of 13 alongside Tessa Thompson. Adrien Brody on the price of winning an Oscar: ‘I abandoned my life’ A tragic legacy — No Other Land, best documentary Basel Adra with his Oscar trophy in the village of At Tuwani, in the West BankFADEL SENNA/AFP via Getty Images Inevitably, of all the categories, best documentary best reflects the world we live in. Last year, No Other Land, about confrontations with settlers in Palestinian villages in the West Bank, triumphed, while the two previous winners were 20 Days in Mariupol (Ukraine) and Navalny (Russian opposition). In the decade before that, most of the factual films were about everything from soul music to climbing, via an octopus. After the glamour of the Oscars, the creators of No Other Land returned to a land ravaged by war. The project was the culmination of work by Palestinian-Israeli activists and laid bare the destruction of communities in the occupied West Bank. In February 2025, just weeks before the ceremony, the co-director Basel Adra was attacked by Israeli settlers in the West Bank. He has remained there in the villages of Masafer Yatta throughout the past year, documenting the impact on his community. “Even after the Oscar, we returned to the same reality,” he has said. In March 2025 the co-director Hamdan Ballal was assaulted by masked settlers in Susiya and detained by the Israeli military. The image of the Oscar-winner blindfolded and handcuffed sparked an international outcry, leading more than 800 Academy members to sign an open letter condemning the industry’s initial silence. He was released 20 hours later. In July, the film’s consultant Odeh Hadalin was shot dead amid settler violence. Hadalin has been called an exceptionally humane and peaceful person. The unlikely Gogglebox star — Kieran Culkin, best supporting actor, A Real Pain The former child star and Succession stand-out Kieran Culkin’s win for A Real Pain felt like a validation of a slow-burn career that, since winning, has kicked on rather fast. He has been cast in the Hunger Games prequel Sunrise on the Reaping, playing a young Caesar Flickerman, a character previously played by Stanley Tucci. Given his quick-witted sarcastic humour — see his acceptance speech for his Screen Actors Guild supporting actor award for A Real Pain — fans of the franchise have rejoiced. Between that, a voice role in Andy Serkis’s upcoming motion-capture Animal Farm, and a surprise viral appearance on Celebrity Gogglebox with his wife, the producer and journalist Jazz Charton, Culkin has also made time to do theatre, starring in a Broadway revival of Glengarry Glen Ross. His portrayal of Richard Roma earned him a Drama League award nomination. The big earner — Zoe Saldaña, best supporting actress, Emilia Pérez Zoe Saldaña in a scene from Emilia PérezNetflix via AP For Zoe Saldaña, the win for her role as Rita Mora Castro in the Spanish musical crime film Emilia Pérez was the accolade she needed for a career that had, of late, been better known for enormous amounts of cash. Because, given her roles in Marvel films as well as the Avatar franchise, by last December, her return as Neytiri in Avatar: Fire and Ash officially cemented Saldaña as the highest grossing actor to date, with her films making more than £11 billion. It is a position that grants freedom and she is now balancing her executive producer duties on the third season of Lioness with a pivot to romantic leads. In May she begins filming Positano in Italy, a Netflix romance film with Matthew McConaughey. Oh, and then there might be Avatar 4. How did Zoe Saldaña become Hollywood’s highest-grossing actor of all time? The champion of Brazilian cinema — Walter Salles, best international feature film, I’m Still Here The director Walter Salles has used his win to champion Brazilian cinema. He spent late 2025 supporting the work of his peers, specifically his fellow director Kleber Mendonça Filho, whose film The Secret Agent is up for best picture at this year’s ceremony. What’s next for him? He is in production on Terra, a film where two brothers embark on a road trip to Patagonia after the death of their father. The prescient one — Peter Straughan, best adapted screenplay, Conclave The British screenwriter Peter Straughan, who won for his adaptation of Robert Harris’s Vatican thriller, has become the go-to architect for Hollywood adaptations. While his 2025 Netflix film Ballad of a Small Player, starring Colin Farrell, barely entered the cultural conversation, February’s star-studded heist film Crime 101, with Chris Hemsworth and Mark Ruffalo, received mostly positive reviews. He has been confirmed as one of the three writers for Sam Mendes’s four-film Beatles cinematic series, along with Jez Butterworth and Jack Thorne. As if that were not enough, he is also in development on his directorial debut, an adaptation of Ned Beauman’s novel The Teleportation Accident with Film4. Read more film reviews, guides about what to watch and interviews And the box office winner… Despite winning only two awards from ten nominations (best costume design and best production design), Wicked has made the most money at £569 million. It was also the third most searched-for film last March. Search peaked again in November, coinciding with Wicked: For Good hitting cinemas. Of the winners, Anora was by far the most searched at the time of the ceremony, perhaps due to the lower profile at the time of its star, Madison, and the director Sean Baker. Conclave had a surge of searches on April 20 and May 4; the death of Pope Francis on April 21 may have had something to do with it. Searches for other nominees — The Substance, Dune: Part Two, Emilia Pérez and The Brutalist — have dropped off over time. The latter two have also earned less than the others, at £12.2 million and £37.9 million respectively. Perhaps Culkin’s SAG Awards dig at Brody’s rambling Oscar speech (“I don’t think there’s any way anyone could hold this [award] for 45 seconds, which is the allotted time, Adrien Brody”) serves as a reminder for this year’s winners — keep the speeches short, glory won’t last for ever. Who do you hope takes home an Academy Award at this year’s ceremony? Let us know in the comments below
